title: Keep direct SQLite access compatible with the application target
goal: Choose a compatible target and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite version before upgrading: use Sqlite 11 on .NET 10 or 11, or deliberately retain Sqlite 10 for a verified earlier-dependency path. RC2 proof; UWP/classic Xamarin native paths remain excluded.

selectionNotes: Direct Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 11 uses net10.0 assets. EF Core 11 separately requires net11.0.
RC2 package evidence, not actual GA verification. UWP/classic Xamarin native paths are excluded.
This 11.0 migration edition does not add a .NET 10 foundation or a .NET Framework catalogue target.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Run the declared net11.0 console application.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared target. Exact sample pins establish observed verification, not a universal installation requirement.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Declared sample language mode; the SQL code uses no new language feature.

frameworks: Standalone Microsoft.NET.Sdk console; no EF Core or web framework dependency.

packages.name: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite
packages.reason: The direct provider's new target boundary is verified at 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105.

packageAssets: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 11 RC2 has only a net10.0 dependency group; Core 11 RC2 has only lib/net10.0. net11.0 selects that compatible asset.
providers: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite11; SQLitePCLRaw 3.0.5 plus SQLite 3.53.4; actual bundled e_sqlite3 SQLite 3.53.4.
platforms: Executed on Windows x64 only. A compatible native SQLite library is required in addition to managed target compatibility.
UWP and classic Xamarin native builds are unavailable in the current bundled route. No UWP/Xamarin, MAUI or other OS/architecture execution is claimed.
renderingModes: Not applicable: console/database operation; no browser or renderer.
constraints: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 11 targets net10.0 only; there is no netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework asset. A net11.0 app can consume net10.0; EF Core 11 is a separate net11.0 requirement.

The net48 retained dependency example builds with SDK10/C#7.3 and Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies 1.0.3, then runs its actual x64 EXE on installed .NET Framework 4.8.1 (release 533509); it is a comparison, not a selectable catalogue target.
The retained net48 package graph does not prove UWP/classic Xamarin compatibility. Native-platform migration and encrypted/custom bundles require separate checks.
prerequisites: Copy all six files for one chosen sample into a standalone directory; run restore/build from that directory so global.json applies. First restore uses nuget.org; offline guidance retrieval does not mean offline dependency setup.

A writable temporary directory is needed. The program creates a unique local database, disables pooling, disposes connections and deletes its database in finally; no account or external service is used.
Samples and lock files are author-maintained, isolated from root package/build inheritance and automatic Renovate updates.
stabilityLimitations: Stable migration contract, demonstrated using pinned .NET11 RC2 SDK/provider artifacts. No experimental API or experimental opt-in is used. Actual GA reconciliation remains pending in the existing release-wide gate.

evidence.scope: Real Windows x64 file-backed SQLite: parameterized apostrophe-containing value, committed insert, rolled-back update, exact value after connection reopen and database cleanup; package asset inspected by Record-SqliteRuntime.ps1.

Compile actual net48/C#7.3 retained provider10 project with SDK10 and locked Framework reference assemblies. Direct EXE execution is a separate record.

Actual Windows x64 Framework EXE on installed .NET Framework 4.8.1, release 533509: parameterized persistence, commit, rollback, connection reopen and cleanup; SQLite 3.53.3. This is execution, not cross-compilation or a mock.

humanProof.scope: Bounded console/provider claims have actual automated Windows x64 compilation and execution, including net48 compiled against 4.8 and executed on installed 4.8.1. No UI/device/Human proof is needed for these routes. UWP/classic Xamarin and other native platforms are excluded, not implied by compilation. Actual GA remains a separate release gate.
